**Triage (R+29)** — first-touch on a bare card ⇒ `pm:queue` · `domain:devx` · `priority:p2` · type `Task`.

**Lands in:** `scripts/check-watch-hint-literal.mjs` (`DECL_NAME`) ⇒ root `scripts/` ⇒ `domain:devx`.

**Type `Task`, ⛔ not `Bug` — and the distinction is the card's own:** the gate's header is careful about what it deliberately does *not* assert, and it **never claims** to cover sibling declaration names. ⇒ this is **incomplete reach, not a stated bound failing**. Contrast #13226 / #13227 (graded `Bug` this week), where the gate's declared invariant — *a value it cannot reduce is REPORTED* — did not hold. Here nothing declared is broken; the scope was simply never argued. ⭐ The card says exactly that: *"this reads as unexamined reach rather than a decided boundary."*

**p2:** nothing red, and the loss is prospective.

## ⚠️ But one unguarded site deserves naming, because it is the guard's own family

Of the four gates the card identifies using `ROOT_FILE_WATCH_HINTS`, one is **`scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs`** — the line ratchet. ⇒ if that declaration were ever tidied into a computed expression, the ratchet would **silently drop out of every dispatch brief** while every local assertion stayed green. ⛔ That is the exact mechanism this gate exists to refuse, applied to the gate that guards the protocol files. Not a reason to regrade, but it is why "prospective" is not the same as "cheap".

⭐ **And the name set is growing while the guard is not**: the card notes #13207's own new declaration (`DECLARED_WATCH_HINTS`, added on the branch this was measured from) is **also** outside reach. ⇒ the asymmetry is not static; each new gate that needs a population constant can invent a name the guard does not know.

## ⛔ The trap to carry into the dispatch

> the gate refuses an empty population deliberately, so **any widening should keep a per-name non-empty floor** — otherwise a renamed constant reports the healthiest green the gate can print.

⚠️ That is the failure this card would otherwise create while fixing itself: widen `DECL_NAME` to a set, someone renames a constant, its entry finds zero declarations, and **a zero population reads as "nothing to complain about"**. ⇒ per-name floor, ⛔ not a global one.

**Not decided here, correctly** — widen `DECL_NAME` to a set of names / derive the names from the extractor / decide the other two names should not exist. ⭐ The third option is worth genuinely considering rather than dismissing: three spellings for one idiom is itself the drift, and consolidating names may be cheaper than teaching the guard all of them. That is a verification-strategy call ⇒ the `domain:devx` seat's, ⛔ not the maintainer's inbox.

⭐ **Dedupe accepted, ⛔ not re-run** — repo-scoped REST list plus local grep over 398 open items, **positive control first** (`watch-hint-literal` → 12 items), then the subject query (`ROOT_FILE_WATCH_HINTS|ROOT_WATCH_HINTS` → 0). A zero with a control ahead of it is the standard.

**Contention:** `scripts/` gate family is hot this week (#13230, #13232, #13233, #13237, #13246, #13251, #13265 all queued or dispatched there). ⛔ This file is not among them, but the `domain:devx` seat clears serial constraints at claim time.

⚠️ **Timing:** the merge queue is deadlocked (#13281, p0). ⇒ weigh arming anything now — the `domain:cli` lane is deliberately holding four accepted PRs unarmed for this reason.

### ⛔⛔ HARD FENCE: `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` is NOT yours this round

The card offers three routes and one of them is *"deriving the names from the extractor"*. I read the tree rather than reasoning from descriptions:

```
extractWatchHints  →  defined at scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs:1807  (73 mentions in that file)
```

⇒ That route lands in a file **claimed in this same batch by #13312**. ⛔ Do not take it. If your measurement says the extractor route is the right one, **STOP and report the fork** — do not edit that file, and do not work around the fence by copying the extractor's logic here.

⭐ Why this fence is spelled out rather than assumed: a prior seat dispatched #13227 and #13233 onto one file after asserting "on a different file" in writing, inferred from the two cards describing different *mechanisms*, never checked. **Different mechanism does not mean different file.**

✅ **The primary route is clear of it.** I read the gate's imports: `node:fs`, `node:path`, `node:url`, `./invoked-as.mjs`, `./js-comment-mask.mjs` — it does **not** import from `dispatch-gates.mjs`. It scans source text for `DECL_NAME` declarations directly (`const DECL_NAME = 'ROOT_DIR_WATCH_HINTS'` at line 94, used to build its regex at 142 and its self-test fixtures throughout). Widening that to a set of names is entirely in-file.

### Zone 1 — ruling

Close the name-scope gap. The gate's mechanism is right and its reach is not: it is keyed to **one** constant name, spelled once, while sibling declarations carry the identical silent-drop mechanism.

⭐ **Carry the card's own guardrail — it is the sharpest thing on the card and it is the vacuity trap this lane keeps paying for:**

> the gate refuses an empty population deliberately, so any widening should keep a **per-name non-empty floor** — otherwise a renamed constant reports the healthiest green the gate can print.

⇒ A widened gate that finds zero declarations for one of its names must **REFUSE for that name**, ⛔ never pass quietly. A guard whose success condition equals its total-failure condition must refuse.

⛔ The card does **not** decide between widening `DECL_NAME` to a set and "deciding the other two names should not exist". The second is a real option — but it is a change to other gates' declarations, ⛔ outside this file surface, so if the measurement points there, **report it rather than doing it**.

### Zone 2 — the counts are claims; re-derive them

Measured on `main` at `74049254`, and `main` has moved several times since:

| declaration name | mentions | guarded |
|:--|--:|:--|
| `ROOT_DIR_WATCH_HINTS` | 136 | yes |
| `ROOT_FILE_WATCH_HINTS` | 41 | **no** |
| `ROOT_WATCH_HINTS` | 8 | **no** |

⚠️ Re-derive all three on your own head. This lane has had figures wrong in both directions, and one card in this very batch measured its own census drifting by a whole helper inside 24 hours.

Also re-check the four named gates said to use `ROOT_FILE_WATCH_HINTS` — `check-doc-anchors.mjs`, `check-required-contexts.mjs`, `scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs`, `check-agent-test-spelling.mjs` — ⛔ **by reading them, not by trusting the list.** A card in this lane recently named a file that does not exist.

⭐ And note the card's own provenance: it was found while implementing #13207, whose new population constant is named `DECLARED_WATCH_HINTS` — a **fourth** name, also outside reach. Check whether that one has landed; if it has, your population is four names, not three.

### Standard

- ⚠️ **Dedup channel is down.** `search_issues` returns FALSE ZEROS. Use `list_issues`; if you cannot dedup, ⛔ file nothing blind, hand findings back in `out_of_scope_findings`.
- ⛔ **No angle-bracket placeholders in GitHub prose** — use placeholder WORDS.
- Capture exit codes **before any pipe**; ⛔ `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` is not safe here.
- ⛔ `git log` / `rev-list` on this shallow clone answers wrongly and exits 0 — use `scripts/pm/git-history.mjs`.
- Prove ablation mutations on disk; predict shapes before running; report predictions you got wrong.
- Convention obligations for editing a gate script: `pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates`, `node scripts/pm/bare-root-worklist.mjs --self-test`, `check-self-test-wired`.
- Derive gate families on your **own final head**. Leave your own claim comment. Report as a comment **here first**.

## ✅ ACCEPT (substance) — PR #13443. ⛔ Landing held on CI convergence, not on any defect.

R31, session `session_01Pk26oZ12t5N1hwGW1m1MgC`. Reviewed against the **diff**, ⛔ not the report's self-description.

**Form:** one file, `scripts/check-watch-hint-literal.mjs`, +321/−60 — exactly the declared surface. ⭐ **`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` is untouched**: the fence held. Draft, `skip-changeset`, ⛔ no governed path, clause ② does not fire.

### ⚠️ My fence was right as an action and wrong in its reason. The dev dissolved it.

I fenced this card off `dispatch-gates.mjs` because the card's *"derive the names from the extractor"* route would land there — and I had verified `extractWatchHints` is defined at `dispatch-gates.mjs:1807`. That much was true. What I inferred from it was not:

> `extractWatchHints` keys on **NO constant name at all** — it masks comments and self-tests, then collects every quoted path-shaped literal in the module body.

⇒ ⭐ **There is no list of names in that file to derive from, so the route I fenced does not exist.** The silent-drop mechanism is a property of the **spelling**, not of any particular constant — which is also the argument for why the roster is the right shape. The dev read the file, edited nothing, copied nothing, and reported the dissolution instead of quietly working around the fence. That is the correct handling of a fence whose premise fails.

### Two card corrections, both found by reading rather than trusting

1. ⭐ **`DECLARED_WATCH_HINTS` has landed** (`packages/spec/scripts/check-llms-txt.ts`), so the population is **four** names, not three. I flagged this as a lead; it paid.
2. ⚠️ **The card's gate list is wrong in BOTH directions.** There are **eight** `ROOT_FILE_WATCH_HINTS` declarers, not "at least four" — and one it named, `scripts/check-agent-test-spelling.mjs`, **does not use that constant at all**: it declares `ROOT_DIR_WATCH_HINTS` and was already guarded. My brief said to re-check that list by reading it rather than trusting it, and that is exactly what it caught.

Counts re-derived on its own head (the card's were five days stale): `ROOT_DIR` 143 mentions / **22** declarations (card said 136), `ROOT_FILE` 41 / **8**, `ROOT_WATCH` 8 / **2**, `DECLARED` 4 / **1** — **33 declarations across 4 names**, all already literals, so the gate is green on landing and the loss it closes is prospective, as the card said.

### The Zone 1 guardrail landed, and it is pinned against the cheaper design

The per-name floor is in, it runs **first** in `main()` (*"a name that found nothing must not be able to reach the pass below on the strength of the names that did"*), and `missingNames()` was split out as a **pure** function specifically so the self-test can drive it without a filesystem — ⭐ *"the vacuity this guards against is the one shape a live-tree assertion can never exhibit while the tree is healthy."* That sentence is the whole reason a green tree could never have pinned this.

⭐⭐ And the counterfactual is asserted, not just the behaviour:

```
t('a global "is the population non-empty" floor would NOT catch it -- which is why it is per-name',
  oneNameGone.length > 0 && missingNames(oneNameGone).length === 1);
```

⇒ The self-test proves the **cheaper design would have missed it**. Also careful: *"a name whose ONLY declaration is unreadable is present, not missing"* — so the same defect is not named twice under two different remedies.

### ⭐⭐⭐ It closed the roster's own rot, which is the mechanism by which this defect arrived

Unasked, and correct: a floor catches a name that **disappears**; it cannot catch one that **appears**. The gate now **discovers** any declaration whose name ends in the idiom's suffix but is not rostered, and refuses it by name. The docblock says why that is not hypothetical — *"the fourth name above was added by a gate written the same week this reach was measured, arriving outside the roster with nothing red."*

⇒ A hand-maintained roster that rots silently is the same species of defect as the single name it replaced, one level up. Fixing the defect **and** the mechanism that delivered it is the right scope, not creep.

The self-reference hazard is handled too: fixtures assemble names from `DECL_NAMES` at run time, and two cases pin that this file holds exactly one declaration site across all rostered names **and** declares no unrostered spelling — so the roster's own string literals are not read back as declarations.

### Ablations: three legs, three distinct mechanisms, no wrong predictions

⭐ Leg **(A)** is the strongest: the same mutated tree run through **both** gates — widened **RED** (`the ROOT_FILE_WATCH_HINTS declaration is COMPUTED, not a literal array`), pre-change gate **GREEN** (`23 ROOT_DIR_WATCH_HINTS declaration(s), every one an array of quoted literals`). The defect measured directly, with the old gate as its own control. (B) isolates the floor, (C) isolates discovery. Self-test 29 → 57 cases.

⭐ Two instrument notes worth keeping: `check-ci-filter-parity` and `check-shard-attestation` first exited 1 with `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` on a fresh worktree with no `node_modules`, then passed after install — *a refusal you can satisfy is not a reading you may keep*, and neither was reported as a finding. And `check:cross-package-test-inputs` **looked silent** because it prints `OK:` rather than a tick and the grep pattern missed it — read as **NOT MEASURED** until the full output was opened, ⛔ never as green.

⛔ It correctly declined to consolidate the four names, with the reason I asked for: that is a change to ten other gates' declarations and belongs to a card that owns those files.

### ⛔ Landing held, only on CI

At `f952a602`: `Test Core (1/6)` `in_progress`, the rest of the suite still converging. ⛔ Nothing here is a rework item; I will arm when every check is green and the six shards read individually.
